[issue_comment] WickedShell | created=2017-02-16T09:58:00Z | updated=2017-02-16T09:58:00Z | https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/5738#issuecomment-280286038
A quick status update on this:

As I was afraid, this fix is not terribly compatible with the M8P support and config saving. Spent quite a lot of time trying to tweak some timing/startup orders, but there isn't a fundamentally reliable solution as presented here with the standing methodology that the autodetect behaves upon. However I've had 2 ideas about how to fix it, one of which is easy and straightforward and I believe will resolve it, the other of which is a much larger (but a long term needed rewrite). I'll give these a stab tomorrow, I just wanted to note that this wasn't ready to be merged in yet.

---

[issue_comment] OXINARF | created=2017-02-16T18:16:41Z | updated=2017-02-16T18:16:41Z | https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/5738#issuecomment-280412969
>As I was afraid, this fix is not terribly compatible with the M8P support and config saving

What is the issue there?

Just to be clear, you think the issues that Peter and other people reported are due to the driver getting destroyed several times before the GPS is properly configured, right?

---

[issue_comment] WickedShell | created=2017-02-16T19:09:00Z | updated=2017-02-16T19:09:00Z | https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/5738#issuecomment-280427653
The issue is that in order to reliably force enough connection info out, we end up enabling messages that we don't want if there is PVT support on the device. This has the knockon effect that by the time we've detected PVT support we've already enabled messages we don't want to have enabled. So we disable them, however because we enabled/disabled these other messages this indicates to us that we need to save the config. This breaks the only save if config changed, because we end up saving every cycle, which is not the desired behavior.

The problem Peter and a couple others have reported (Confirmed on peter's side at least because we dumped config and I can now reproduce it). Is that his GPS is in a very unusual configuration state. He has NAV-VELNED enabled, but doesn't have NAV-POSLLH (which is not a ublox factory default configuration, or how 3DR ever shipped units). The instance was detected because the NAV-VELNED is a valid message to be receiving. The old driver used to hammer the GPS immediately with a number of config lines designed to force the essential messages on. Because of the above issue with the M8P and config saving this was removed from master.

So what I'm looking to arrive at is a solution that can detect if we have PVT support reliably, and if we don't then set the config as fast as possible. The solution I mentioned that requires more work but is the best, is to change how we manage losing GPS's. Right now we consider it lost if we haven't received a valid position message for 2 seconds (which on anything without PVT support means 2 messages are required), we unload the driver. That's actually a really bad behaviour. The ublox driver can recover as long as the baud rate hasn't been changed, so what we actually would prefer is to unload the driver if we haven't received *any* valid messages from the GPS. The key distinction being if we are receiving anything from the GPS (and we are prompting it for responses), then we still have a valid instance and will recover, rather then hooking off the position message. This is a larger rewrite to the GPS frontend/backend split however so I'd like to try the easier solution first that could be easily backported to the Copter 3.5 and Plane 3.8 releases without much hassle.

---

[issue_comment] OXINARF | created=2017-02-16T23:00:20Z | updated=2017-02-16T23:00:20Z | https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/5738#issuecomment-280491438
Thanks for so much detail Michael. The hard solution we had already talked about in the PR that enabled PVT, that's really the best one. You haven't said what is the easier fix you are going to try, so my question/suggestion is if we couldn't ask the version first and from there determine what messages to ask for? I mean, we already have to wait for the version to be fully configured, so what is the downside to not do any configuration requests until we have the version? You think it wouldn't be fast enough?

---

[issue_comment] WickedShell | created=2017-02-20T04:06:56Z | updated=2017-02-20T04:06:56Z | https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/5738#issuecomment-280983522
Alright, at this point I'm comfortable with the changes. A quick summary of them:
- Reconfigure the required nav rate, velned, posllh, and status. This is required to keep a poorly configured GPS connected. This is the primary problem that @peterbarker encountered. However the rate is also a really important fix.
- GPS driver timeout has been raised to 4 seconds. This is required for allowing the ublox driver enough time to get the above items reconfigured in time. This means that losing a GPS driver will take longer to be detected and restart the process, but this already needs to not be happening in flight.
- AP_GPS_UBLOX::_send_message() now checks that it can fit a message in the Tx buffer and returns false if it doesn't manage to write an output. This hasn't shown up as a issue to date, however we need to protect against this, as GPS injection could be filling the Tx buffer for us.

This needs to be backported to the Plane 3.8 and Copter 3.5 releases to correct for some poorly configured GPS units.

---

[issue_comment] OXINARF | created=2017-02-24T18:44:46Z | updated=2017-02-24T18:44:46Z | https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/5738#issuecomment-282370790
@WickedShell I couldn't finish my re-review before this getting merged and the PR looks good, but here go some possible improvements:

- port is required for PVT and SOL, but those two are supposedly requested first (they won't if we don't have port already). Is port something that is sent to us even before we try to request any configuration? I think putting the port as the first request would reduce some delays
- the request of the version isn't checking if message is sent or not (and the method is only used in one place so it could be inlined)
- same for port request
- same for SBAS configuration request
- now that *_send_message* checks if message will fit in Tx buffer, we could remove other checks doing the same in several places of the code, with the most important being in the *_request_next_config* that checks for the biggest possible message instead of the message that would effectively be sent at that moment

---

[issue_comment] WickedShell | created=2017-02-25T00:47:07Z | updated=2017-02-25T00:47:07Z | https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/5738#issuecomment-282444056
@OXINARF It should probably be earlier on the list, but if you look at the implementation of _request_message_rate() if we don't have a valid port yet the first thing we do is fetch the port and return false on having sent the request. This actually means we are ensuring the port first. It would have no impact on the delay or startup time, but would be clearer that that is actually always happening very early.

Good call on version. Port you have a valid point, but as pointed about above we've actually already forced the port request. Still should be made to be consistent however.

Valid point that it can be removed, although thats only after a thorough audit we've covered the other options. I think we have, but it needs to be explicitly checked as I'm not 100% confident on that.

---

[issue_comment] OXINARF | created=2017-02-25T00:59:32Z | updated=2017-02-25T01:00:11Z | https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/5738#issuecomment-282445503
@WickedShell 

> It should probably be earlier on the list, but if you look at the implementation of _request_message_rate() if we don't have a valid port yet the first thing we do is fetch the port and return false on having sent the request. This actually means we are ensuring the port first. It would have no impact on the delay or startup time, but would be clearer that that is actually always happening very early.

I'm aware that it fetches the port first - that's why I said PVT and SOL are *supposedly* requested first. About the delay what I meant is that the port is requested before anything else and then is requested again on its own step (and that step is even before POSLLH and VELNED rates are requested). So, in a configuration requests' first round, port is asked twice - and at the second one we, for sure, already have the port; that's the delay that could be removed.

> Valid point that it can be removed, although thats only after a thorough audit we've covered the other options. I think we have, but it needs to be explicitly checked as I'm not 100% confident on that.

Yes. I've gone through it, but not with review eyes.

title: Improved INS timing
body:
This fixes a major bug in the LSM303D driver, which was using an incorrect sample rate for its accelerometer data for calculating delta-velocity.
It also fixes all drivers sample rates. It splits sensor drivers into two types. FIFO based drivers use a learned sample rate to account for clock differences between sensor and system board. non-FIFO based drivers use the system clock to calculate deltaT.
This significantly improves data quality, and as a side effect it allows non-lock-step SITL backends (such as XPlane10 and FlightAxis to fly properly with EKF as primary estimator)

An example of this is a periodic spike in latency followed by a smaller offset of the opposite sign over several frames. If you truncate the spike, then the average will be distorted.

title: EKF3: Fix range beacon fusion bugs
body:
**BACKGROUND**

The EKF3 uses a multi-hypothesis filter to resolve the height ambiguity when using range beacons that are co-planar in the horizontal (All beacons are at the same or similar height). This filter calculates the vertical position of the range beacons relative to the EKF origin using two hypothesis, one where the beacons are below the flight vehicle and one where they are above. The hypothesis with the most stable vertical position is used. The stability is calculated by low pass filtering the magnitude of the vertical offset changes resulting from each range measurement fusion.

**CHANGES**

This fixes the following bugs:

1) The vertical position calculated by the multi-hypothesis filter was only being updated when the hypothesis selection changed between upper/lower.
2) The hypothesis filer was using range beacon positions that had already had an offset applied which was creating a circular dependancy and reducing stability of the estimate
3) There was an typographical error in the LPF used to filter the upper hypothesis vertical position change.

The following improvements were made:

1) The default LPF filter constant was reduced to allow the hypothesis to change more rapidly so that when a flight vehicle  ascends past the beacon constellation plane, the correct hypothesis can be selected sooner.
2) Spike protection was added to the LPF input.

**TESTING STATUS**

@OXINARF Regarding secondary compasses, they are usually not good, they could be close to PDB's etc, and that won't trip until after the vehicle is trying to fly. Users will disable _USE parameters to get through arming checks if they need to, but most users aren't just disabling all their poor installation location compasses. As for the nullptr, I think it is primarily to do with a signal to the EKF that it should fall into the non compass mode, although realistically it should be able to make that determination internally rather then relying on an external caller setting the compass to null.

[issue_comment] priseborough | created=2017-08-01T20:46:45Z | updated=2017-08-01T20:46:45Z | https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/6703#issuecomment-319491850
The ekf requires both _ahrs->get_compass()->use_for_yaw and _ahrs->get_compass to be true

[issue_comment] OXINARF | created=2017-08-02T18:50:01Z | updated=2017-08-02T18:50:01Z | https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/6703#issuecomment-319763681
@WickedShell @priseborough My main surprise comes from two things:

- in a very recent dev call @tridge said it wasn't really interesting anymore to detect external compasses first; although we still do it in most cases, there is no guarantee for it. This means that anyone using Plane/Rover and that doesn't change the PRIMARY parameter can end up using only an internal compass
- I'm a bit surprised that the EKF isn't able to determine if it should be using a secondary compass and the vehicle needs to forbid the EKF to use them. I also think that it is possible the EKF will switch to a secondary compass if it thinks the one it is using isn't giving good data - so it doesn't even look coherent.

---

[issue_comment] priseborough | created=2017-08-02T21:56:22Z | updated=2017-08-02T21:56:22Z | https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/6703#issuecomment-319810375
If the magnetomer the EKF is using times out, the EKF does look for another valid magnetometer as reported by  _ahrs->get_compass()->use_for_yaw(instance) being true. It is up to the compass library to indicate which magnetomers are available via the use_for_yaw(instance) accessor.

This is about risk management. If the EKF already has acceptable velocity innovations indicating a valid yaw estimate and the compass fails (I'm talking about loss of data failure), then we have two options with different risk factors:

1) Do nothing and don't use a compass. For platforms doing occasional (ie once every minute) velocity changes, this will be OK. For sustained hover or long distance straight-line fixed wing flight, this will build up yaw error which could lead to toilet bowling on copters or a GPS reset event at the next turn for fixed wing. 

2) Switch to a secondary compass which may not have been previously tested in flight. This has the risk of immediate (30 seconds or less) loss of heading reference if the vehicle is hovering at low altitude and hasn't yet transitioned to 3-axis mag fusion. For up and away flight it is likely switching to a bad mag will result in  it continuously failing innovation checks and loss of yaw  is less likely but still possible.

title: COPTER: Fix MOUNT_CONTROL command yaw response
body:
In response to MAV_CMD_DO_MOUNT_CONTROL or MSG_MOUNT_CONTROL in guided mode, or DO_MOUNT_CONTROL in missions.... If the mount instance doesn't support camera panning, the copter is supposed to yaw instead.  For some reason, this was missing from the GCS and Mission commands handling.  So in both guided and missions, the gimbal would tilt correctly, but copter yaw never moved.  I'm surprised nobody noticed this bug, but MOUNT_CONTROL probably has a fairly limited set of users.

These two patches implement the copter yaw when the mount instance does not have panning support.  It does so by calling the same yaw controller that CONDITION_YAW uses.  I've tested this repeatedly, and it worked as intended.

This will close https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/issues/6272

title: Copter/Rover/Plane/Tracker: fix velocity sent in GLOBAL_POSITION_INT message
body:
This PR fixes two things to do with the sending of the GLOBAL_POSITION_INT message to the ground stations and companion computers:

- for all vehicles, fix velocity z-axis field in GLOBAL_POSITION_INT to be in NED format (i.e. +ve is down) to be consistent with the mavlink protocol (http://mavlink.org/messages/common#GLOBAL_POSITION_INT).
- for sub, rover and copter, use the system time instead of the last GPS fix time.  This is correct because our position comes from the EKF not the GPS.  We also get the velocity directly from the AHRS object instead of the inertial-nav library (which we plan to remove and is just a shim on the underlying EKFs)

The only known downside to these changes is the velocity for Rover, Sub and Copter will not appear in the GLOBAL_POSITION_INT message until the EKF has initialised.  It is possible we could fall back to the GPS velocities in case the EKF does not have a good velocity estimate but I don't think this is necessary.  The GPS position and velocities are already available through the GPS_RAW_INT message (albeit using ground course and ground speed instead of a 3D vector)

title: Rover: waypoint navigation sets origin to prev waypoint or stopping point
body:
This resolves issue (https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/issues/7796).

When Rover begins towards the next waypoint, it must initialise both the origin and destination.  Master currently sets the origin to the vehicle's current location which causes the vehicle to drive slightly off the line between waypoints.  This PR fixes the issue by using the previous destination if we've reached it recently.

The improvement is especially obvious if the WP_RADIUS is set to a large number like 10m as shown below.

title: AC_AttitudeControl: Prevent DCM fallback from triggering a flyaway
body:
Plane can fallback to DCM, which will cause `_ahrs.getLastPosDownReset(alt_shift);` to return 0 and not fill in alt_shift. If the vehicle started with the EKF the comparison for `reset_ms != _ekf_z_reset_ms` passes and we dereference `alt_shift` even though it's garbage on the stack. Simplest fix is to special case that returning 0 (which is what happens when an AHRS doesn't implement the method) is invalid.

This really indicates however that we should not be using timestamps, as the uint32_t will eventually overflow.

Large thanks to clang's static analysis for finding this.

title: Rover: remove jump forward when transitioning from forward to reverse
body:
This PR fixes a bug in which the Rover would jump forward for a moment when this was done:

- driver drove vehicle forward towards a barrier in ACRO mode
- avoidance feature caused vehicle to stop before hitting the barrier
- pilot attempted to backup vehicle by pulling throttle down but the Rover would jump forward for a moment before backing up

The cause of the problem was:

- when the driver quickly changes from demanding forward movement to backwards movement, because of acceleration limiting done in the AR_AttitudeControl::speed-to-throttle-output method, the desired-speed used might still be positive.
- the avoidance feature was running off the driver's input (not the acceleration limited input) meaning it would be checking what was behind the vehicle instead of continuing to check what was in front of it

The fix is to apply the acceleration limiting to the pilot's desired speed before performing avoidance.

*beforee (with Jump)*
![master-with-jump](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1498098/39081393-90b3f4bc-457b-11e8-80ab-b9a574040b84.png)

*after (No Jump)*
![new-without-jump](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1498098/39081398-9a132cda-457b-11e8-905c-f5cab274bd66.png)

This PR also:

- enables simple object avoidance for Guided and Steering mode
- removes a small jerk when stopping or transitioning from forward to reverse

title: TradHeli Swashplate Servo Trim Fix in Copter 3.6
body:
This PR is being submitted to fix a bug found with the swashplate servo movement relative to trim.  If the servo is not in the center of the servo range, the movement is based on a fraction of the remaining throw of the servo.  The swashplate relies on the coordinated movement of the three servos.  Thus if each servo had a different trim position, a collective input request will cause the swashplate to be tilted due to the requested fraction of movement would result in different PWM output because each servo has a different remaining throw from trim.  This issue is further discussed [here](https://discuss.ardupilot.org/t/improper-handling-of-swashplate-servo-trim-causing-unequal-cyclic-output-from-one-side-to-the-other/27886)

This PR fixes this issue for single and dual heli frames.  I don't know enough about quad heli frames to know whether this is an issue.  

This fix was tested in the SITL for proper functionality for both single and dual heli frames.  Chris and I have flight tested it on our heli's with no issues.

title: AP_Arming: Restrict GPS/AHRS difference to a 2D solution
body:
The check is attempting to constrain that the GPS and AHRS position are similar, if you are using GPS as your altitude source then the check behaves quite reasonably. However if you are using baro (the default) and have not turned on origin drifting (also the default behavior) if your GPS vertical position has shifted since the EKF origin was set (which happens easily on plane at least) the reported altitude won't track this. If you start the vehicle with a poor initial fix (that is later improved by gaining more correction data/moving to a better signal environment) it's quite easy to trigger the check. We should only be checking the 2D positions are tracking.

We could check the 3D position if we checked that the EKF was drifting the position to follow GPS on height, or if GPS was the primary height reference. I left that out as scope creep for this PR. Resolves #7644 and helps me stop going crazy.

title: Rover: fix forward-back acceleration limiting
body:
This PR fixes [this issue](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/issues/8426) found in [this discussion](https://discuss.ardupilot.org/t/skid-steer-mower-overshooting-pivot-turns/28910).

The issue was that when first engaging the speed controller, we were not acceleration limiting the desired-speed, instead we simply let the desired-speed jump up to whatever the caller requested.  With this change, in these situations we limited the desired-speed using the vehicle's current speed as a base.

To test this change was correct, a SITL rover was loaded with a very simple mission (just one waypoint) and then soon after arming, the vehicle was switched from MANUAL mode to AUTO.  Below is a graph of the desired speed vs actual speed and we can see in the "BEFORE" image that the desired speed immediately spikes up to the WP_SPEED (set to 5m/s) while in the "AFTER" image it rises more slowly.

![before-after](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1498098/40216653-008bc710-5aa3-11e8-927c-67cebb83c0cd.png)

Yes, this method of calculating "dt" isn't good because it leads to jitter in the "dt" value caused by changes in calculation time. Instead we should be passing in a dt value or taking it from the scheduler (if we are happy to assume that this function will always be run at the vehicle's maximum rate).

title: Rover: allow steering to Motors beyond -1 to +1 range
body:
This PR attempts to resolve and issue with loss of steering control for vehicles traveling at high speeds.  This issue was caused by [this earlier PR](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/8312) which moved the speed-scaling from the attitude controller to the motors library.  The potential issue was recognised and sadly now it's been confirmed during beta testing.  Comments from the PR are copied below:

> the potential downside of the change is that at very high speeds the steering control may become so limited that it cannot counteract a physical misalignment in the steering linkage. For example at 20m/s (70km/h) only 5% of the total steering range is available. **A potential solution to this though is to allow steering inputs > 1.**
> 

This PR resolved the problem by allowing the high-level steering request sent to the motors to be outside the -1 to +1 range.

Below are images before and after showing the simulated vehicle is better able to achieve the desired turn rate.  In this test an Ackermann style rover (i.e. separate throttle and steering controls) was driven slowly (2m/s) but with full left steering.  In master, because the speed scaling, the steering output was scaled back too far to achieve the desired turn rate.  With this PR the vehicle comes much closer.

![master-turnrate](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1498098/41139637-d9aad618-6b23-11e8-8060-58aa65a00b7f.png)
![new-turnrate](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1498098/41139638-db769d74-6b23-11e8-9d96-7be20f00a8f0.png)

Somewhat separately this PR also adds a new parameter MOT_SPD_SCA_BASE (i.e. "Motor Speed Scaling Base") which is equivalent to the similar "Vector Thrust Scaling Base" parameter.  It allows the user to specify the lowest speed that the scaling is applied.  I don't expect many people to change this but it could be useful especially for very slow vehicles because it will give them better steering control below 1m/s.  Very fast vehicles that spend very little time below 1m/s.

This issue is discussed [here in the Rover-3.4.0-rc1 beta testing thread](https://discuss.ardupilot.org/t/rover-3-4-0-rc1-released-for-beta-testing).

title: AP_Follow: Initialize offsets based on offset type (attempt 2)
body:
This PR is built upon [PR 8971](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/8971) but fixes a couple of things.

This PR resolves [issue 8915](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/issues/8915) which highlighted that the FOLL_OFS values (which holds where the vehicle should drive/fly to relative to the lead vehicle) were not being initialised properly when the FOLL_OFS_TYPE was "relative" meaning relative to the lead vehicle's heading.

This PR also fixes the AP_FOLLOW_OFFSET_TYPE_RELATIVE definition.

This has been tested in SITL.  The way I tested it was to:

- override the AP_Follow::get_target_location_and_velocity() method to always return AHRS home.
- overrode AP_Follow:_target_head to be 90 degrees (to simulate the vehicle pointing east)
- drove a rover about 30m north of home
- set OFS_TYPE = 0/NED and switched to follow mode and checked that FOLL_OFS_XYZ were set correctly for OFS_TYPE = 0/NED.  I.e. X=30, Y=0.
- switched back to manual, reset OFS_OFS_XYZ to 0,0,0, param fetch
- set OFS_TYPE = 1 (relative) and switched to follow mode again and checked that FOLL_OFS_XYZ was set correctly, i.e. X=0, Y=-30
- also during these tests, I could see the following behaviour seemed correct, After switching to follow the vehicle did not try to drive anywhere because it was already sitting at the right place because the offsets had been initialised to be the current location

title: Plane: Respect frame type on VTOL_TAKEOFF commands
body:
This makes the handling of `MAV_CMD_NAV_VTOL_TAKEOFF` correct to the spec, makes it consistent with the handling of `MAV_CMD_NAV_TAKEOFF` and reduces the possibility of a perceived fly away if an absolute altitude mission is uploaded at any non sea level location. Probably most importantly: it allows for restarting the mission once in flight without the plane deciding to climb the entire takeoff height again if it is above the height.

This has been tested in SITL with absolute, and relative altitude takeoffs.

I think this may cause problems. Last I checked MP only supports a whole of mission frame type. So you don't get the flexibility to pick a different frame for takeoff. For users of MP that have AGL missions they could get a real surprise if their terrain data isn't perfect, even triggering a crash. If they are currently flying with missions that are absolute then updating to a fw with this change could trigger a crash (trying to transition at zero altitude).
If we are going to change this then I think we'd need to add in some protections. For example, if we're not flying when a VTOL takeoff starts, and it is an AGL takeoff, then we'd assume ground level is where we are.
We also could consider a parameter giving the minimum climb height for a vtol takeoff.
For mission restart in flight, I think we should handle that with some tests that check if we appear to already be flying (either with is_flying or similar) and skip the takeoff.

title: Quadplane: Don't send trim values to VTOL motors
body:
Plane (and tracker, although it's not a safety issue there), were calling the `output_trim_all()` function. Unfortunately this results in emitting the channels trim value on motor outputs. If you have the safety disabled this will result in motors spinning during initial boot (with the initial values).

In the following screenshot Channel 0, 1, 3 are motor outputs, Channel 2 is the forward motor, channel 4 and 5 are tied to auxiliary pins used as GPIO. (Channel 4 goes low before calling `BoardConfig.init_safety()` channel 5 goes low when it returns)
![untitled 1](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/567688/44449535-48892580-a5a3-11e8-90d5-ae48fdfab70a.png)


Channel 0 is going to 1.549 ms pulses which is the trim value on that channel. With the patch applied rebooting instead looks like this (Channel 4 and Channel 5 are debug and were removed):
![untitled](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/567688/44449109-12977180-a5a2-11e8-99f7-1e8e11cd0e10.png)

There is also a safety bug where if the FMU fails the IO processor will configured to emit trim values, which on quadplanes are quite unsafe as well. This takes the approach of not configuring them, which brings plane into symmetry with copter on handling the VTOL motors. (Only applies to PX4 builds since ChibiOS does not provide a failsafe setup yet)

Finally based on a conversation with @rmackay9 and a weak understanding of copters code I can't see a particular reason for us to need to set the trim values when we will shift into normal generated values shortly anyways. We can limit this to only trim the non VTOL surfaces as well, but as Randy pointed out the current behavior would cause you to moved something like landing gear on boot immediately, which isn't good either.

All testing thus far has been based on a Cube + PX4/FMUv3 builds.

title: Copter: booster output respects safety switch
body:
Copter-3.6 (and higher) support a "booster" motor for multicopters ([blog](https://discuss.ardupilot.org/t/petrol-boosted-tricopter/17823)).  These are configured by setting SERVOx_FUNCTION to 81 (boost_throttle) and then setting MOT_BOOST_SCALE to a postive number from 0 to 1.

This PR enables the output to the booster to reflect the safety switch instead of enabling it along with other "auxiliary" outputs (used for gimbals, etc).

This has been tested on an mRobotics Pixhawk1 under NuttX:

- connected a servo tester to read the output from MAIN OUT 5 of the pixhawk
- set MOT_BOOST_SCALE = 0.5, SERVO5_FUNCTION = 81
- rebooted pixhawk
- with safety switch unpressed (disengaged?), no PWM pulses were sent
- with safety switch pressed, PWM values were output (same value as held in SERVO5_MIN)

This item was reported in [this Copter-3.6 beta testing thread](https://discuss.ardupilot.org/t/copter-3-6-0-rc7-released-for-beta-testing/31513/10).

P.S. I'm not totally overjoyed with the complexity of implementing the get_motor_mask() in the AP_MotorsMulticopter class and then calling it from all the children.  I considered two other alternatives before implementing it this way:

- modify each child class's get_motor_mask() function to include the boost channel (overall less code actually).
- add a get_motor_mask_multicopter (or similar) and force the children to override this method instead of get_motor_mask (this would remove the need for the children to call the parent).

title: Rover: fix G_Dt when SCHED_LOOP_RATE increased
body:
This fixes a bug in the G_Dt calculation (which is used in the motors library and PID controllers) when the SCHED_LOOP_RATE is increased above 50hz.  It also resolves this issue related to mavlink data being sent too quickly: https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/issues/9262

The problem is the scheduler.get_last_loop_time_s() function returns immediately (with an incorrect dt) if nobody has consumed the IMU samples since the previous loop (I don't 100% understand the issue but this is close).  Rover's scheduler had the update rate for the ahrs_update task set too low (50hz) meaning it was not being run on every iteration.  Also it's estimated time was too high (1500ms) which led to it not being called sometimes.

This PR:

- corrects the problem by reducing the ahrs_update time to 400ms which is the same Plane.
- increase the rate of the ahrs_update and some other critical functions to 400hz so they always run when SCHED_LOOP_RATE is increased.  The update rate could be increased even higher (i.e. 1kHz) but in reality we don't expect people to raise SCHED_LOOP_RATE above 400hz.

This has been tested in SITL and on a real board.  Below is a screen shot of the G_Dt values from a Pixhawk1 running at 50hz, 100hz and 200hz loop rate respectively.
![beforevsafter](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1498098/44615899-9d68bc80-a87f-11e8-8816-4a85d8602793.png)

title: EKF: Fix bad roundoff and inconsistent altitude handling
body:
This addresses the #9420 reported by @horiuchi4dn. The core problem this is trying to address is accidentally forcing the getLLH method of the EKF to always be rounded to 1 meter. This was less serious then it sounded as any call through `AP_AHRS::get_position` full reset the altitude anyways, but it can propegate into `AP_AHRS::get_location()`.

This corrects this by moving the logic that `AP_AHRS_NavEKF` was applying to live inside of the getLLH method and doesn't require get_position to do the reset. This has 2 side effects:
- `getLLH` could return true before even if we didn't have a valid vertical position (`get_position` couldn't so this should be minimal impact, and those places I can see that are affected actually benefit from the protection). 
- `getLLH` was not correctly applying the `posOffsetNED.z` correction which means that `getLLH` was returning incorrect results if you had an offset accelerometer. Again it's a small change that I believe is correct and won't affect most locations.

Final note: I'd like to remove `AP_AHRS::get_location()` but I will probably leave that for a separate PR.

EDIT: Worth noting that this should improve reported position error in replay as replay was using getLLH to compare the error.

title: Rover: proximity and avoidance fix
body:
This PR fixes a few issues found while setting up simple object avoidance to work with ROS. The fixes are:

- remove the proximity checks from the Rover arming checks.  For copters these proximity checks mostly so that the pilot is aware of objects on the frame itself that may be obstructing the proximity sensor.   These obstructions could stop the vehicle from being able to move in certain directions after takeoff.  With Rovers this problem is much less important.
- ROS/mavros can provide OBSTACLE_DISTANCE messages to the AP_Proximity library but the update rate (even on an NVidia TX2) seems to be relatively low and irratic so I've increased the timeout to 0.5sec.  There are of course better solutions (such as improving the performance somehow of the ROS/mavros portion) but in general, I think the 200ms we had before was too low.
- AC_Avoid bug fix when using the "stop" method.  When looking for the intersection point with a polygon boundary we need to include the "margin" or else we will often not find the intersection point until long after the vehicle should have started slowing down.
- AC_Fence change to *not* return the 1st point in the _boundary array which is the "return to" point (that copter never uses).  This fix resolves an issue introduced by [this PR that was just merged to master](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/8790).

The AP_Avoid and AC_Fence changes should be included in Copter-3.6 although most Copter users stick with the default "slide" object avoidance.

This stop avoidance using a 360 lidar has been tested on a real rover.  The polygon fence change has been tested on a Copter in SITL.

title: AP_RangeFinder: Benewake sends max-range+1m when out of range
body:
This PR corrects two issues discovered during Copter-3.6.1-rc1 testing ([see discussion here](https://discuss.ardupilot.org/t/copter-3-6-1-rc1-is-available-for-beta-testing/34787/9)):

- The Benewake lidar driver returns the RNGFND_MAX_CM + 1m if the lidar goes out of range.  Previously it would ignore these readings but this would lead to the lidar's state becoming "NoData" when really it's "OutOfRangeHigh".  The 1m addition to the defined maximum range is a bit arbitrary but I wanted to ensure that it's significantly beyond the maximum so that no rounding errors could lead to it being considered within range.  Below is a screen shot of a test where the RNGFND_MAX_CM was set to 1500 so the lidar reports 16m when out-of-range.

![benewake-test](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1498098/48174157-22755500-e34a-11e8-981e-0b0b42082fce.png)


- Copter's extended system status message to the GCS reports the lidar as healthy as long as it's returning data.  Previously the lidar was only reported healthy if the lidar range was within the MIN and MAX.  In my view, "healthy" means the lidar is operating as expected and no action is required from the user.  It's a normal and expected thing in most situations that the lidar will go out of range of the ground so I don't think it's good to report the lidar as "unhealthy" in these situations.
symptom: Benewake sends max-range+1m when out of range

title: AC_PosControl: set-alt-target-with-slew sets desired to 0 once at target
body:
This resolves an issue with the AC_PosControl::set-alt-target-with-slew() method which was leaving the z-axis **desired velocity** at the max speed-up or speed-down when the vehicle had reached the target altitude.  This method is only used in RTL when the RTL_ALT_FINAL != 0 (i.e the vehicle will hover a couple of meters above home instead of landing).

Leaving the desired velocity incorrectly set causes a jump in the climb rate and throttle when the user switches to another mode (like Loiter).  It causes a jump because Loiter uses z-axis "feed forward" so the old desired velocity was momentarily being used.  It is also related to Loiter (and other modes) not fully resetting the position controller's state because it views the position controller as "active".

This issue can be reproduced in SITL by doing the following:

- set RTL_ALT_FINAL = 200
- arm and takeoff to 10m in Loiter, return rc3 to 1500 (mid stick)
- switch to RTL mode and let vehicle descend to 2m
- switch to Loiter
- the twitch is visible in both the CTUN.ThO and CTUN.DCr

Below is a graph from the desired climb rate before and after the fix
![rtl-to-loiter-twitch-before-after](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1498098/48962946-eee22e00-efcb-11e8-808e-fe7868a0c4da.png)


This issue has been [discussed here in the forums](https://discuss.ardupilot.org/t/throttle-drop-when-switching-to-loiter-from-rtl/34388/43).

title: AP_Mount: fix extreme gimbal movements before TX is turned on
body:
This PR resolves a long standing issue with the Mount library ([issue reported here](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/issues/6096) and [here](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/issues/2426)) in which the gimbal would move to either it's extreme edge or, in the case of the SToRM32 gimbal, even outside of it's defined acceptable range.

The fix is:

- check that the RC input isn't 0.  It is only zero when the transmitter has not yet been turned on.
- when converting RC input into a target angle constrain the input to the channels defined min and max input range.

Images below show the before and after of a Mount setup with a single Tilt servo on Output channel 9.  The Pilot controls the tilt angle with RC input channel 6.

title: Follow: fixed handling of FOLL_SYSID
body: and add an example follow script for Morse rovers
comments:
[issue_comment] rmackay9 | created=2018-12-07T01:14:42Z | updated=2018-12-07T01:27:22Z | https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/9963#issuecomment-445088356
Here's a bit of odd behaviour I think we will see with 3 vehicles which have sys-id 1,2 and 3.  In this example, the intention is for rover3 to follow rover1.

- on rover3, FOLL_SYSID == 0 at the beginning so _sysid_to_follow = true and accidentally rover2's global position message arrives first so_sysid = 2
- user sets FOLL_SYSID = 1 to make rover3 follow rover1
- data from rover1 stops arriving, timeout happens and rover3 goes back to following rover2

I think the behaviour we want is:

- if FOLL_SYSID == 0 then vehicle locks onto first vehicle it "sees"
- if data from followed vehicle stops arriving, vehicle goes back to original status waiting for another vehicle.  once it "sees" a vehicle again (could be a different vehicle or the same vehicle as before) it locks on again and starts following
- if user sets FOLL_SYSID to a non-zero value then the following vehicle must detect this and stop this auto-detection behaviour until the user resets FOLL_SYSID to zero.

title: UAVCAN driver task priority
body: @hsteinhaus, the issue of UAVCAN communication latencies we investigated recently (caused by incorrect task priority configuration) causes severe sensor measurement delays which will make some UAVCAN-interfaced sensors perform poorer. I suggest to increase the UAVCAN task priority to `SCHED_PRIORITY_ACTUATOR_OUTPUTS` per your  proposition, despite that fact that it breaks APM arming at the moment. Anyway the arming problem is likely going to need a solution unrelated to task priority settings.

title: uORB multi pubsub depends on order of subscribing/publishing
body:
Below is what I found, correct me if I'm just wrong :):

Basically, I think, in the current multi pubsub implementation, the publisher needs to be started before the subscriber, otherwise they won't talk to each other.

An example from #2297 would be:
1. Mavlink starts first and wants to subscribe to the distance_sensor topic. It gets the first instance here:
   https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/blob/master/src/modules/uORB/uORB.cpp#L144
2. The the ll40ls wants to do a advertise_multi:
   https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/blob/master/src/drivers/ll40ls/LidarLitePWM.cpp#L116
   https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/blob/master/src/modules/uORB/uORB.cpp#L93
   I believe this fails here:
   https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/blob/master/src/modules/uORB/uORBManager_nuttx.cpp#L246
   And gets +1 here probably:
   https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/blob/master/src/modules/uORB/uORBDevices_nuttx.cpp#L471
3. This leads to mavlink subscribing on 0 and the ll40ls publishing on 1.

Instead of the check ...
- Does the node exist already?

It should be something like:
- Does the node exist already and has stuff been published yet?
- Does the node exist already but is it only opened by a subscriber?

Apart from hardware issues discussed [here](https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/px4users/bI1-ZbecoN8), there is also software bug. The target field is uint16. According to specs it's supposed to contain milliamps \* 10. This suggests that the source field contains milliamps, but as far as I can tell it actually contains amps. This would match the effect we saw for currents between 0 and 15 amps.

The scaling for the MAVLink message changed during the last commit.

title: Line calculation for POSCTL, convergence north/south
body:
@tumbili as discussed

I've observed this previously but didn't follow up on it (https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/issues/2299). When testing variations on runway takeoff we also used the same calculation to draw a line with current heading. It resulted in a wrong actual heading during takeoff:

![screen shot 2015-10-21 at 08 47 56](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/5750020/10768340/debad4d4-7ce0-11e5-963d-50cabaf7f6b5.jpg)

The blue lines were calculated by the posctl method, the red line is were it actually should be. Note that both lines match for 90 degrees.

Example calculations (posctl method):

```
Origin: 47.389492,8.0317354

160:
Point behind:
47.389492 - cos(160degrees) * 100/1e6 = 47.3895859693
8.0317354 - sin(160degrees) * 100/1e6 = 8.03170119799

Point ahead:
47.389492 + cos(160degrees) * 3100/1e6 = 47.3865789529
8.0317354 + sin(160degrees) * 3100/1e6 = 8.03279566244

90:
Point behind:
47.389492 - cos(90degrees) * 100/1e6 = 47.389492
8.0317354 - sin(90degrees) * 100/1e6 = 8.0316354

Point ahead:
47.389492 + cos(90degrees) * 3100/1e6 = 47.389492
8.0317354 + sin(90degrees) * 3100/1e6 = 8.0348354
```

Solution:
The calculation we actually want can be found here (great circle distance): http://www.movable-type.co.uk/scripts/latlong.html (part "Destination point given distance and bearing from start point")

We can update posctl to do the following:
- calculate the 2 waypoints with bearing and constant distance (a few hundred m)
- before we reach it, calculate new actual bearing at the end of the line
- use the new bearing for the next pair of waypoints

title: Special handling for manual control inputs for large heading errors
body:
As soon as the heading error becomes large (often the case for VTOL in high winds) the manual roll and pitch controls do not lead to the reaction the user would expect. This is because the roll and pitch sequence comes after the yaw sequence in the euler formulation we are using (we are generating the attitude setpoint quaternion from euler angles).
However, this is tricky for the user and should be fixed.

- move to land

title: Passthrough mode for Snapdragon on PixFalcon fails to output PWM
body:
I am using a PixFalcon in passthrough mode to control the ESCs with the Snapdragon flight.
The PixFalcon refuses to talk to the ESCs, which beep every few seconds as a result.

I am seeing this on the current master (af02b860b3cc495f67a879088dca9f8b1edd58f9) with the following procedure:
Flash the firmware to the PixFalcon
`make px4fmu-v2_default upload`
With the SD card out, connect to the NuttShell. Set a normal airframe and reboot:

```
param set SYS_AUTOSTART 10020
reboot
```

Once rebooted, re-connect, press the safety switch and test the PWM:

```
pwm test -c 1 -p 1200
```

The motor turns, the ESCs are quiet.
Set the passthrough airframe and reboot (via the nsh command, **not** power-cycling):

```
param set SYS_AUTOSTART 20000
reboot
```

Re-connect and test the PWM (safety switch not required)

```
pwm test -c 1 -p 1200
```

The motor turns, the ESCs are quiet. If I `reboot`, the PixFalcon's LED will now light up purple instead of blinking blue, but `pwm test` still works.

As soon as I power-cycle, `pwm test` no longer works (and neither does `snapdragon_rc_pwm`).
After stopping `pwm test` with `Ctrl-C` I get the following message:

```
pwm: PWM_SERVO_SET(0): Invalid argument
```

I see the same output printed in [`snapdragon_rc_pwm`](https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/blob/2f48317a9ea7b05d8c61b3d1c44f8229491350b1/src/drivers/snapdragon_rc_pwm/snapdragon_rc_pwm.cpp#L209), where `ret == -1` and `errno == 22`.

title: Descend mode when GPS fails needs checking
body:
The case where RC and GPS, both have failed, needs to be checked. It should go into open-loop descend mode, however, it doesn't seem to execute it correctly and just drifts off.

Additionally, it can't auto-disarm after landing because the landing detector doesn't work when GPS is lost.
comments:
[issue_comment] tubeme | created=2016-05-16T21:26:55Z | updated=2016-05-16T21:26:55Z | https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/issues/4534#issuecomment-219553369
Probably this is the reason I had almost terrible accident with a friend of mine. My VTOL flipped after rough landing, far away in pretty deep grass. So in the rush I did not disarm the machine thinking that auto disarm will trigger. My friend went to pick up the VTOL, He saw that the machine is upside down spinning the props on idle. Once he picked up the machine it gave full throttle in his hands. It was almost fatal. I heard the props but was away from my RC. Finally I was able to disarm. But THIS IS DANGEROUS! It happened probably because when flipped the VTOL did not have GPS reception. I could not find the reason until now and could not explain how is it possible that the auto disarm did not trigger for 3 minutes obviously on the ground flipped over.


---

[issue_comment] julianoes | created=2016-05-17T13:42:05Z | updated=2016-05-17T13:42:05Z | https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/issues/4534#issuecomment-219720897
@tubeme I don't think that your issue is directly connected to the GPS fail (unless a log proves it). If it flips, the impact is likely to throw off the position estimator, so it might just not have detected the landing.
I agree that it would be good if an upside down landing would get detected properly, it's something to chase up in a separate issue.

However, I would argue that the "danger" in this case clearly came from approaching and picking up a vehicle when it is still armed.

@jgoppert I did a git bisect and it points me here: 97e6a57501e58b3151300dcaa8d7215d9a47eb9c

As I understand it, the following happens:
1. Local position is not published by LPE without GPS
2. The position control loop doesn't run because it does `continue` [here](https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/blob/master/src/modules/mc_pos_control/mc_pos_control_main.cpp#L1239), so it doesn't pass on the manual input.
3. The attitude control loop doesn't get manual input.

@tumbili : Why does the manual input need to go through the position controller in manual mode?

@julianoes Some time ago the attitude setpoint was generated both in the position controller and in the attitude controller. After that we moved the setpoint generation into mpc only. The cleanest way would probably be to have the stick mapper module publish the setpoint but that is nowhere near to be completed.

[issue_comment] jgoppert | created=2016-06-08T13:31:48Z | updated=2016-06-08T13:41:05Z | https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/issues/4766#issuecomment-224589367
@tumbili LPE has a flag LPE_GPS_ON, if it is set to 1, it expects that a GPS is connected, and will wait to initialize the altitude until enough GPS readings have been received. If LPE_GPS_ON = 0, then it will allow baro to initialize the altitude. The issue was that the baro initialization was typically happening first and all sensor offsets were being calculated relative to baro instead of GPS which is generally more accurate.

title: Drift when estimating attitude on Snapdragon eagle platform
body:
Hi,
I'm noticing drift / poor attitude estimation on the Snapdragon eagle platform. For example, if I flip the drone on its back, it takes a few seconds to settle and find the correct attitude. Similarly when I flip it back, the roll angle will be wrong by up to 45 degrees and only slowly correct. What parameters can I tune to fix this? I've already tried changing parameters in Attitude Q estimator via QGroundControl but these changes don't seem to affect it.
EDIT: it actually uses the ekf2 estimator on the qurt side despite SYS_MC_EST_GROUP. So ekf2 seems to be drifting.

- The pointer being set (shmem_info_p) and the one being used later on where actually different variables (had a different address).
- The reason for that is because shmem_qurt.c is linked in twice: this file ends up in `build_qurt_eagle_default/src/platforms/qurt/px4_layer/libplatforms__qurt__px4_layer.a` which is added to `build_qurt_eagle_default/src/firmware/qurt/libpx4.so` but _also_ erroneously to `build_qurt_eagle_default/src/firmware/qurt/libpx4muorb_skel.so`!

The actual issue is WAY WAY worse, not only is shmem_info_p duplicated, all static and global variables in all 'modules' that are added to libpx4.so are duplicated:

```
"drivers__device;modules__sensors;platforms__posix__drivers__df_mpu9250_wrapper;platforms__posix__drivers__df_bmp280_wrapper;platforms__posix__drivers__df_hmc5883_wrapper;platforms__posix__drivers__df_trone_wrapper;platforms__posix__drivers__df_isl29501_wrapper;systemcmds__param;modules__attitude_estimator_q;modules__position_estimator_inav;modules__local_position_estimator;modules__ekf2;modules__mc_att_control;modules__mc_pos_control;modules__param;modules__systemlib;modules__systemlib__mixer;modules__uORB;modules__commander;modules__land_detector;drivers__gps;drivers__pwm_out_rc_in;drivers__qshell__qurt;lib__controllib;lib__mathlib;lib__mathlib__math__filter;lib__geo;lib__ecl;lib__geo_lookup;lib__conversion;lib__terrain_estimation;lib__runway_takeoff;lib__tailsitter_recovery;lib__DriverFramework__framework;platforms__common;platforms__qurt__px4_layer;platforms__posix__work_queue;modules__muorb__adsp;df_mpu9250;df_bmp280;df_hmc5883;df_trone;df_isl29501"
```

being the list of object archives (.a) that are added to both, libpx4.so and libpx4muorb_skel.so

http://stackoverflow.com/questions/31503597/cmake-link-a-shared-library-to-static-libraries

I think this is the real problem: you cannot add STATIC libraries to SHARED libraries the way it is currently done in the project.

title: get() doesn't fetch a new param value if previous value was 0 unless rebooted
body:

title: RTL allows user take over without mode switch
body:
RTL kicked in (set to 50 meter radius), and it brought the drone home and during landing user wanted to nudge the x-y position a bit, but as soon as they touched the sticks the drone immediately switched to stabilize mode, and drone started to plummet until user realized and ramped up throttle to catch the free fall.  I love the idea of being able to nudge the drone while landing (like Solo) but it would be nice if this didn't turn off auto-landing.  This was using latest PX4 master bits from 1/25/2017 with ekf2.

See [log description ](http://www.lovettsoftware.com/Downloads/Bugs/RTLIssue.png)and [actual PX4 log](http://logs.uaventure.com/view/6MLvpYmTqh7N5YerRHjRug).
comments:
[issue_comment] dagar | created=2017-01-27T00:09:49Z | updated=2017-01-27T00:09:49Z | https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/issues/6444#issuecomment-275553958
So the intention is that after a geofence breach you should be able to easily continue your flight after RTL brings your vehicle back within the boundary.

Options that immediately come to mind.

 1. only allow mode revert to happen for some defined time after the geofence breach (eg 10s)
 2. RTL land actually initiates LAND mode. The mode change would invalidate the possibility of geofence escape and indicate to the user that that you're landing.

As far as tweaking the landing via stick input, that type of thing has been debated off and on. I personally like the idea of any AUTO mode ignoring user input. If you want to land like this why not switch to position mode instead?

---

[issue_comment] lovettchris | created=2017-01-27T02:23:19Z | updated=2017-01-27T02:23:19Z | https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/issues/6444#issuecomment-275574099
Fair enough, my assumption was RTL was a type of auto mode, so I was surprised by the difference in behavior here.  The 3DR solo allows x-y tweaks during landing - it's a nice way to ensure you land right on the launch pad, which is handy in rough terrain.  I would be fine with RTL working like other auto modes requiring mode switch to take control - as it is a bit too easy to bump the sticks accidentally and not realize what you did until the drone hits the ground...  I realize one can learn these things, but the question then is what will new users expect...

---

[issue_comment] AndreasAntener | created=2017-01-27T07:24:52Z | updated=2017-01-27T07:24:52Z | https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/issues/6444#issuecomment-275604676

But, I would also be fine with disabling this, needing to flick a switch forth and back seems like a good alternative.
I wouldn't switch to land for the position shift, but rather reuse the implementation for both.

---

[issue_comment] dagar | created=2017-01-28T18:03:14Z | updated=2017-01-28T18:03:14Z | https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/issues/6444#issuecomment-275863762
@AndreasAntener for 1) what do you mean "at least you would see that it's doing something"? Right now the mode does change and is announced in a default QGC setup. There are also mavlink critical messages.

For land I'm talking about the land phase of RTL actually switching to the land navigator state, but that's kind of a separate discussion. 

If this is causing confusion (even among experienced users) I'm not opposed to deleting it.

---

[issue_comment] tubeme | created=2017-01-28T20:28:32Z | updated=2017-01-28T20:28:41Z | https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/issues/6444#issuecomment-275872523
I think the problem is the drastic difference in the modes between auto and manual. If it switches to Position mode then there should be no problems given now you can land in Positition mode.

[issue_comment] dagar | created=2017-01-28T20:47:34Z | updated=2017-01-28T20:47:34Z | https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/issues/6444#issuecomment-275873602
The use case imagined was a casual flyer or FPV racer flying and blowing past the geofence, brought safely back within the fence via RTL, and then wanting to easily regain control by wiggling the sticks to resume whatever mode they were in previously. 
Now I'm thinking a mode change to break out is likely good enough and less confusing.

[issue_comment] AndreasAntener | created=2017-01-29T10:44:38Z | updated=2017-01-29T11:53:51Z | https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/issues/6444#issuecomment-275906137
> @AndreasAntener for 1) what do you mean "at least you would see that it's doing something"? Right now the mode does change and is announced in a default QGC setup. There are also mavlink critical messages.

doesn't work if you don't have your GCS with you

> For land I'm talking about the land phase of RTL actually switching to the land navigator state, but that's kind of a separate discussion.

yes I know but I think this would make the state switching in commander more complex

[issue_comment] dagar | created=2017-01-29T18:35:46Z | updated=2017-01-29T18:35:46Z | https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/issues/6444#issuecomment-275935338
Ah, I keep forgetting that people actually fly without a GCS sometimes. Good point.

---

[issue_comment] lovettchris | created=2017-01-30T19:34:16Z | updated=2017-01-30T19:34:16Z | https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/issues/6444#issuecomment-276165842
It would be safer if the stick bump switched to POS CTRL.  I agree user can learn it is doing this from the heartbeat and/or statustext.  The reason I filed this bug is I was mostly worried about crashing the drone accidentally by bumping the sticks during RTL when no other auto-mode will behave that way.  POS CTRL should solve that.  But it begs the question, why not allow this take over on any auto mode for consistency.  Conversely I would argue if it is not good for every auto mode then why is it good for RTL?   I would still like to nudge on landings, but I'll file that as a separate issue.  

---

[issue_comment] dagar | created=2017-01-30T19:40:19Z | updated=2017-01-30T19:40:19Z | https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/issues/6444#issuecomment-276167517
I'm now thinking about getting rid of this behaviour altogether, but I'll try to explain what's currently happening.
It's not allowing the user to regain control in any RTL, it allows a user that was in a manual mode (manual, altitude, position, acro, etc) and breached a geofence to quickly retake control and go straight back into the mode they were in. So this only happens if you have geofence action set to RTL, or LOITER/HOLD and you're in that mode as a result of a geofence breach.



---

[issue_comment] LorenzMeier | created=2017-01-30T20:01:17Z | updated=2017-01-30T20:01:17Z | https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/issues/6444#issuecomment-276173509
I'm thinking in an opposite direction: Rather than trying to get rid of it to switch to the closest mode available with manual input, which is POSCTRL. This makes sense for planes and multicopters and VTOL.

Wanting to adjust / abort the landing can make sense in a lot of situations. But rather than having two pilots, allowing the human to take over is much more consistent.

---

[issue_comment] lovettchris | created=2017-01-30T20:04:29Z | updated=2017-01-30T20:04:29Z | https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/issues/6444#issuecomment-276174378
Speaking of two pilots, see my [new feature request](https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/issues/6483).

Daniel's explanation makes sense, I can see how that is useful if you expect that behavior.  So it allows take over as soon as it enters the fence?  could have some interesting battles between manual and RTL right over that boundary then :-)   

So here's where it was confusing.  While still outside geofence, sticks did nothing.  So one thinks they will continue do nothing until RTL is finished (or you do a mode switch).  How does one know from a long distance away it has re-entered the fence anyway?  (Perhaps there's a status message to this effect? Perhaps we should announce the user can now resume flying or something like that)...

But I could just as easily flip a mode switch to get control back...like I can do with other autonomous modes already.  I can see this could be a religious argument.  Just thought I'd bring it up since we nearly crashed our drone not realizing this was happening.  Flipping to pos control would be safer.



---

[issue_comment] dagar | created=2017-01-30T21:14:13Z | updated=2017-01-30T21:14:32Z | https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/issues/6444#issuecomment-276192507
The geofence action won't trigger faster than once every 10 seconds. So if you violate the fence it will immediately switch to RTL (depending on GF_ACTION), you could then retake control right away and stay outside of the fence, but then 10 seconds later it would trigger again.

To summarize, could I have your feedback on a specific solution here? @lovettchris @LorenzMeier @AndreasAntener @tubeme 

 - keep geofence failsafe escape functionality via wiggling sticks, but with changes...
   - only escape to position control mode, anything else could be dangerous
   - better user feedback
   - documentation! (QGC setup screen, and guide)
   - possible timeout? If RTL triggers as a result you can only retake control via stick movement for the next < 10 seconds before it's just regular RTL

[issue_comment] julianoes | created=2014-02-24T20:37:20Z | updated=2014-02-24T20:37:20Z | https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/issues/649#issuecomment-35932737
@thomasgubler and I did some more investigations on this today:
The observation is that "sometimes" loiter (whether mission without mission, loiter or RTL) lets fixedwing dive pretty scary.

This happens even though airspeed is working fine and the altitude setpoint is correct. Our theory is now that the groundspeed undershoot is calculated incorrectly in the case of loiter (see here: https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/blob/beta/src/modules/fw_pos_control_l1/fw_pos_control_l1_main.cpp#L716)
Since the distance to the loiter WP is used to calculate the groundspeed undershoot, this most probably leads to a huge "desired airspeed"  which then makes the tecs controller dive in order to gain velocity.

The current proposed workaround is to set groundspeed undershoot to 0 in loiter:
75c6706278119e50ce56ecbb1620025a9b9b936d
909e138182000350df19d47367d6f68d0a6b7fd4

This hopefully solves this case for now, testing has yet to prove it.

On a side note, I also think that the plane should never be allowed to dive like this, even if it can't reach a waypoint because of strong wind. It should rather be pushed away by the wind than crash, right?


---

[issue_comment] LorenzMeier | created=2014-02-25T16:34:01Z | updated=2014-02-25T16:34:01Z | https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/issues/649#issuecomment-36026948
@julianoes @thomasgubler I agree on the dive part. I'm not sure if this is a parameter tuning issue or the TECS implementation is suboptimal in that case.
Do you guys have a log of the dive? Does the system go full throttle on dive? If it does, we need to limit the groundspeed undershoot to a reasonable value. If it doesn't go full throttle, then we might need to do something about this part.

I think your workaround is sensible, but it would be great to understand the issue fully here, so that we do not run into it again in a different flight mode.


---

[issue_comment] julianoes | created=2014-02-25T21:16:07Z | updated=2014-02-25T21:16:07Z | https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/issues/649#issuecomment-36058991
@LorenzMeier: Yes we do have a log of a dive, I've already had a thorough look at it. We do immediately get full throttle during the dive. Basically, it should stop pitching down if it's already at full throttle. I think I also read comments in the code in that direction, maybe it's something that has been commented out.

The workaround has been flown successfullly today on the X5, no dive issues so far!

title: Takeoff not detected after 2nd time in altitude mode
body:
Hello
With release v1.6.0rc1 or the current master the takeoff seems not to be detected after the second time arming in altitude mode:
http://review.px4.io/plot_app?log=b29f4633-e7c9-49a9-ab92-18106d9f01f9

```
2017_02_23_09_31_15: [logger] file: /fs/microsd/log/2017-02-23/09_31_1
2017_02_23_09_34_09: ARMED by RC
2017_02_23_09_34_11: Takeoff detected
2017_02_23_09_34_29: Landing detected
2017_02_23_09_34_31: DISARMED by auto disarm on land
2017_02_23_09_34_36: ARMED by RC
2017_02_23_09_34_46: DISARMED by auto disarm on land
```
The first time arming in altitude, the takeoff and landing is detected fine.
After the 2nd time arming, the motors are only spinning with idle thrust for some seconds and the attitude/position controller is not responding to any rc commands or nick/roll movement.
In case I switch to e.g. stabilized mode and then back to altitude mode again (when the motors are spinning with idle thrust) the takeoff is detected, the motors are spinning up and the attitude/position controller seems to be working again.

title: RTL mode state is not being reset to NONE
body:

On some case it is, if for example a mission is being triggered on between.

2) fly to another location (you must fly, another bug is that RTL is not started if triggered just after takeoff)
3) start RTL 
4) the drone will climb (RTL_STATE_CLIMB)
5) the drone will return home (RTL_STATE_RETURN)
6) the drone will start descending (RTL_STATE_DESCEND)
7) pause the drone
8) fly to another location
9) start RTL again
10) (BUG here) instead of starting the RTL from beginning (step 4) it will continue from it last state (in this case descending)

its much more critical if during RTL mode its goes as far to RTL_STATE_LAND mode. 
its seems that a call to set_can_loiter_at_sp(true) should be done on some places on the code (which I am not sure where)

title: LandDetector Bug
body:
Can't take off after the first flight in Altitude mode.
Because of this line:
https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/blob/master/src/modules/land_detector/LandDetector.cpp#L206
This line will never works until we leave landed state:
https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/blob/master/src/modules/land_detector/MulticopterLandDetector.cpp#L214
So,if we arm in altitude mode ,this line will be the only chance to takeoff:
https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/blob/master/src/modules/land_detector/MulticopterLandDetector.cpp#L239
It's looks good for the first time to takeoff.
But,when we landed and disarmed after the first flight.
_min_trust_start !=0 after we landed,because we returned from https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/blob/master/src/modules/land_detector/MulticopterLandDetector.cpp#L204  ,and we did not reset "_min_trust_start"  to zero.
In this case ,we can't takeoff after the first flight if we are in altitude mode with no position lock.

Maybe we could never takeoff if we are in altitude mode and have position locked?

I'll make a PR now with the `RotateVector()` fix, but I can change that to flipping the declination's sign if you think that's more appropriate in the review.

title: Takeoff overshoot in real world but not in the simulator
body:
When I ask the drone to take off to 5 meters it shoots aggressively up to 10 meters then comes back down:
![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/18707114/24180121/4e9fbc48-0e70-11e7-8c1c-51aff459651c.png)

[14-25-29-input.zip](https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/files/860207/14-25-29-input.zip)

Looking at the code in mc_pos_control, around line 1561 under the comment "special thrust setpoint generation for takeoff from ground" I see that it ramps up throttle all the way to MPC_THR_MAX if necessary in order to get the drone off the ground, and when it detects drone has reached MPC_TKO_SPEED speed then it switches to normal setpoint altitude hold.  The problem I see with this is that the GPS sensor is very slow, so it always cranks to MPC_THR_MAX for very agressive takeoff.  

I want to fix this, but I could use some pointers.  I don't want any new parameters, we already have too many, instead I would love the code to be self tuning, for example, if I strap something heavy on my drone, it should "just work".  I assume that the current behavior came about because you also do not want the drone to "hop" during takeoff because then it thinks it has landed again and disarms.  

But clearly from the picture above, PWM shot all the way to up max throttle (90% of 1950 is 1755) before it even detected drone leaving the ground, then because the acceleration was so great, even with PWM falling quickly to 1283, the drone was essentially flung up to 10 meters.    What is very interesting is the red line I drew on the PWM signal.  Drone is still ascending quickly, and PWM is going up??? from 1283 to 1443.  I realize you don't want the drone to freefall, but there must be something wrong there.

So I propose to add a takeoff that is more gentle, like landing.  Where it slowly spins up the props just to get some idea of what it takes to get any vertical acceleration.  For example, when I look at the charts, z-mag responded 1 full second before GPS noticed any change.  In fact, z-mag was seeing something when PWM was way down at 1100.  This slow ramp up ensures safety, if anyone is near they will back off before it shoots up into the air.  So from there it should ramp up quickly to HOVER_THROTTLE + some delta, where that delta is self tuning.  This sudden ramp will cause a hop, but to keep it in the air we need more than hover throttle, so it can start more aggressively to ensure no hops, but then it will write a private setting to calibrate this value so that the next take off will be smoother and smoother each time you try it.  This is a little bit like auto-tuning a PID algorithm I suppose.

Any objections or better ideas ?

[issue_comment] Stifael | created=2017-04-13T16:03:24Z | updated=2017-04-13T16:03:24Z | https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/issues/6876#issuecomment-293939730
That sounds reasonable. But how do you know hover thrust. As default it is set to 0.5, but the actual hover thrust can easily be below it. That is where the integrator comes on, which corrects for the wrong hover thrust. But you dont know that before actually being in air.

[issue_comment] MartinSollie | created=2017-04-16T13:05:49Z | updated=2017-04-16T13:12:07Z | https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/issues/6876#issuecomment-294350859
I think the problem with takeoff overshoot comes from the hover throttle feedforward added in 5529023 that is not taken into account in the takeoff code:
```C++
// copter has reached our takeoff speed. split the thrust setpoint up
// into an integral part and into a P part
_thrust_int(2) = _takeoff_thrust_sp - _params.vel_p(2) * fabsf(_vel(2));
```

Try something like this instead:
```C++
_thrust_int(2) = _takeoff_thrust_sp - _params.vel_p(2) * fabsf(_vel(2)) - _params.thr_hover;
```

If you reduce the P and I velocity gains from the default in the simulator you can probably see the overshoot there as well.

title: Possible Bug in HIL_STATE_QUATERNION handling
body:
Hi,
@TSC21 and I are developing HIL plugins in MAVROS. This is to allow any ROS-compatible simulator to be used in HIL setup.

In the decoding of HIL_STATE_QUATERNION msg, in PX4 firmware, specifically the ```vehicle_global_position```,
https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/blob/ecb2511a7bbad094bff23dd95036eda0656778f0/src/modules/simulator/simulator_mavlink.cpp#L402-L413
altitude is divided by ```1E3```, but ```lat/lon``` are not scaled down properly. In the msg definition,
https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/blob/912ed98a28022504ef3ec4bf1bce0fe041f83ac4/msg/vehicle_global_position.msg

```lat/lon/alt``` are assumed to be in deg/deg/meters. And, they are supposed to be received in deg 1E7 and meters 1E3 according to 
https://pixhawk.ethz.ch/mavlink/#HIL_STATE_QUATERNION

So, I guess that 
https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/blob/ecb2511a7bbad094bff23dd95036eda0656778f0/src/modules/simulator/simulator_mavlink.cpp#L407-L408
should be divided by 1E7.

Also the ```vehicle_global_position``` msg does not have ```timestamp``` field,

So, possibly another mistake here,
https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/blob/ecb2511a7bbad094bff23dd95036eda0656778f0/src/modules/simulator/simulator_mavlink.cpp#L404

Thanks.

> Also the vehicle_global_position msg does not have timestamp field,

> So, possibly another mistake here,
https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/blob/ecb2511a7bbad094bff23dd95036eda0656778f0/src/modules/simulator/simulator_mavlink.cpp#L404

title: Yaw/thrust saturation and loss of control during flight
body:
Hi everyone,

During a position control flight with my VTOL (in MC mode only), I encountered a really strange behavior. After flying perfectly well, the yaw control was suddenly lost and the drone was loosing altitude.

![esc_response2](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/14822839/26549616/2bc1ae62-447a-11e7-81eb-4d79c5c93205.png)

As you can see, around t=59s, the drone did not respond to the yaw command even if the ESC reported acceleration and deceleration of the motors. After that between t=63s and t=69s, the drone is spinning around it's yaw axis and since it was loosing altitude, the thrust did reach saturation, without any RPM response.

I'm suspecting a mixer saturation or an ESC issue. 

Link to the complete [log](http://logs.px4.io/plot_app?log=55960095-7efd-4e28-8acc-1854828e75bc).

Finally, my setup is a PixHawk Pro with Orel 20 ESCs and a mRo GPS.

New log from this morning, same issue after less than 3 minutes. 
Same sequence: 
1. No yaw response to the motors ramping up and down (t=[167,170]s)
2. Altitude loss 
3. Thrust saturation

I maybe found the issue in the `mixer_multirotor.cpp` file ([link](https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/blob/master/src/modules/systemlib/mixer/mixer_multirotor.cpp#L326-L337)).
```
} else if (out > 1.0f) {
			// allow to reduce thrust to get some yaw response
			float prop_reduction = fminf(0.15f, out - 1.0f);
			// keep the maximum requested reduction
			thrust_reduction = fmaxf(thrust_reduction, prop_reduction);

			if (fabsf(_rotors[i].yaw_scale) <= FLT_EPSILON) {
				yaw = 0.0f;

			} else {
				yaw = (1.0f - ((roll * _rotors[i].roll_scale + pitch * _rotors[i].pitch_scale) *
					       roll_pitch_scale + thrust + boost)) / _rotors[i].yaw_scale;
}
```
When the output saturates, the `thrust_reduction` is computed but the new yaw value is then computed again with the old unreduced thrust. The final result is then a reduced thrust with no yaw control.

@sanderux, I dont really want to take the credit for the altitude limit, because I dont like to have it in the landdetector either and would like to remove it. However, I dont know how geofence works right now and not sure if I have the time to work on that. What I can do right now is to limit the mission  altitude to the max altitude...

[issue_comment] Stifael | created=2017-06-11T16:31:14Z | updated=2017-06-11T16:32:12Z | https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/issues/7309#issuecomment-307640437
@LorenzMeier I am in favor of turning off the landdetector alt max for now, since in order to implement it properly it requires some more changes. Currently the landdetector adjusts max altitude based on battery level. Lets assume the vehicle is flying a mission. It is possible to adjust the desired altitude to the max altitude, but what happens if the vehicle is in between two waypoints and the battery level goes below the threshold which results in a lower max altitude. The navigator  already has set the current waypoint and does not know about the altitude max change and will therefore set a mission altitude above the max.
In order to solve that, the navigator also needs to know when the max altitude has changed and then update the mission item accordingly. However, before I implement something like that I prefer to clean up the navigator first such that waypoints are actually only sent when they have changed.
with turning off I mean set the alt max to a very large value and do not apply any altitude adjustment based on battery

here is a branch where I moved the altitude limit to the navigator and removed the altitude limit from the position controller and land-detector.
https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/tree/pr-limit_altitude_navigator

the reason why I did that:
- a detector should just detect an event, but should not apply any action as it was done in the land-detector for altitude limitation
- the battery level is already handled/detected by the battery.cpp class. Hence, it is not necessary to do another detection in the land-detector

it is to note that the altitude limitation in the navigator only applies for mission related maneuvers such as mission, rtl etc. It does not work yet for repositioning such as altitude change and go-to, because unfortunately they are  handle differently. The problem is the LOITER exit here - https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/blob/master/src/modules/navigator/mission_block.cpp#L374

> @bkueng what do you think about dumping the original dataman mission items to logger? Then adding something to pyulog to output a .mission file? I know they're already on the sdcard, but I can think of many occasions where this would have been extremely helpful.

Interesting. I agree this can be helpful. I see some difficulties with an actual implementation though:
- reading from dataman (SD card) will block, which can lead to logging dropouts. It can be reduced by splitting the reads over multiple loop iterations, but might still be an issue, and can take a while for larger missions.

-  Then we would also need some standardized format so that changes to the dataman structs won't break the parsing in pyulog.
