title: FW Land mode = crash
body:
I recently had a flight that put up a "[commander] failsafe: no global position warning", then switched to Land mode and proceeded to fly straight into the earth. My main concern is why the global position was lost in the first place (did the estimated position and gps position begin to differ too much? why?), but it would be nice to know that there is a reliable FW solution for this sort of condition to return to the ground hopefully in one piece.

Log here: http://logs.px4.io/plot_app?log=b7fcb8a9-a66f-4b49-94e3-f896d3a65cb7
comments:
[issue_comment] JonReacher | created=2017-07-13T04:05:13Z | updated=2017-07-13T04:05:13Z | https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/issues/7609#issuecomment-314964724
I know there are several ways that you could go about returning to the ground as safely as possible. In this particular case it seems that if the autopilot would have trusted the gps and disregarded position estimation everything would have been fine. If it truly is flying blind, or thinks it is, and no dead reckoning is available, would it be best to go into a descending loiter at a slow target speed, say FW_LND_AIRSPD_SC?

---

[issue_comment] dagar | created=2017-07-13T04:39:53Z | updated=2017-07-13T04:39:53Z | https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/issues/7609#issuecomment-314968755
There's an open loop loiter GPS failure mode, but I'd rather use the FW position controller to execute a heading hold landing while controlling airspeed. The main blocker to this at the moment is the FW position controller (TECS + L1) runs based on global position updates. I'm thinking of how to refactor it to continue running TECS.

---

[issue_comment] Antiheavy | created=2017-07-18T16:08:09Z | updated=2017-07-18T16:08:09Z | https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/issues/7609#issuecomment-316113824
A more typical loss of GPS failsafe in the world of fixed wing UAVs is to spiral down so as to hit the ground as close to the last reported GPS location as possible.  If you just heading hold you will likely get blown far downwind before hitting the ground - from 400 feet altitude a typical fixed wing might glide for over a mile downwind.

I'd vote for something like this:

1) Loss of GPS failsafe timeout ( 0.5 to 10 seconds depending on how long the given system can be expected to safely operate without GPS and/or without global position from the EKF).
2) Failsafe trigger
3) Set throttle = 0
4) Spiral down slowly holding airspeed: set to cruise speed or maybe minimum speed, hold a fixed bank angle
5) if GPS regained switch to Hold mode


---

[issue_comment] dagar | created=2017-07-18T18:47:52Z | updated=2017-07-18T18:47:52Z | https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/issues/7609#issuecomment-316161069
Thanks, I forgot about actually needing to find the plane after it safely lands.
If you were in a mission when you lost GPS and then it came back shouldn't the mission resume?

[issue_comment] Antiheavy | created=2017-07-18T20:57:19Z | updated=2017-07-18T20:57:19Z | https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/issues/7609#issuecomment-316195419
> If you were in a mission when you lost GPS and then it came back shouldn't the mission resume?

hmmm...  yeah, maybe you are right.   I'm thinking about if the vehicle descends down low and then decides to turn and start resuming the mission in some bad direction right into some trees or something, then again I don't know that Hold mode would be any better.   Less confusing to just resume whatever it was doing previously I suppose.  

---

[issue_comment] JonReacher | created=2017-07-19T22:20:38Z | updated=2017-07-19T22:21:25Z | https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/issues/7609#issuecomment-316535841
I very much agree with spiraling down. Linear landing is scary for many reasons. A plane in a linear descent with a shallow glide angle can cover some serious ground before hitting who knows what.  At least with a descending loiter you have a reasonable expectation of the general "terrain" it will land in. The alternative may travel away from a safe flying area to the next town. I fly on a ridge with a small city visible in the distance below a few miles away. One failsafe could set it on a course for real trouble.
  Is it too simple to just use the GPS failsafe navigation settings for the global position loss, except maybe with a scaled down throttle setting to ensure slow descent?  These should already be set for a holding loiter, at a reasonable radius for the specific aircraft.
  I'm no coder, but could you point to those parameters in case of a failsafe, then add a percent scale down, for example?

---

[issue_comment] priseborough | created=2017-07-31T03:15:41Z | updated=2017-07-31T03:15:41Z | https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/issues/7609#issuecomment-318957529
The current practice of fixed wing failsafe going into an open loop control mode is dangerous and often results in a high speed spiral dive, endangering people on the ground and providing little time for recovery. 

For fixed wing vehicles I would like to see addition of a CIRCLE_DESCENT mode that enables the plane to be put into a zero throttle, constant bank, constant pitch condition to provide a controlled slow speed spiral descent. If we assume that only the attitude solution is valid, then we cannot use TECS, so controlling to a specified pitch angle will be required. 

The only time the open loop mode should be used as the failsafe for fixed wing is when the attitude data in the control state message is invalid.



---

[issue_comment] Antiheavy | created=2017-07-31T04:16:00Z | updated=2017-07-31T04:16:00Z | https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/issues/7609#issuecomment-318963334
> If we assume that only the attitude solution is valid, then we cannot use TECS, so controlling to a specified pitch angle will be required.

2 cents: if valid airspeed (and baro altitude for that matter) are present they should be used instead of constant pitch.



> fixed wing failsafe going into an open loop control mode is dangerous and often results in a high speed spiral dive, endangering people on the ground

here is a recent fixed wing flight log where this exact spiral dive happened resulting in destruction of the vehicle:
http://review.px4.io/plot_app?log=1c1b7c69-d55c-4f63-a287-85d5be996453

[issue_comment] priseborough | created=2017-07-31T04:21:17Z | updated=2017-07-31T04:21:17Z | https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/issues/7609#issuecomment-318963852
The existing speed and height control loops (TECS) requires derivative states that are not available from using Baro or GPS directly, so until TECS algorithms are modified to generate this data internally, attitude control will have to do and will be a lot better than what we have currently.

[issue_comment] priseborough | created=2017-07-31T05:17:39Z | updated=2017-07-31T05:17:39Z | https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/issues/7609#issuecomment-318970098
I've been working on a progressive series of improvements to make the ekf faster to recover from a loss of navigation caused by bad magnetometer data. https://github.com/PX4/ecl/pull/294 a resulted in significant improvement in the ability to handle bad compass data and https://github.com/PX4/ecl/pull/313 will result in further improvements in that area when it has been tuned and tested.

The major remaining challenge is how to handle bad inertial data caused by excessive vibration levels. This can strike without warning in flight when RPM changes and structural resonances are excited and can make inertial navigation impossible.  What we need in that instance is a fallback mode that make minimal use of the accelerometer data. Until we disable the DLPF in the IMU and perform all digital processing in the driver, we will not be able to reliably detect clipping in the inertial sensors.

title: Manual Overwrite not allowed in Stabilized Flight Mode
body:
While testing the v1.6.5 of the PX4 Firmware I discovered that in the stabilized mode the manual overwrite is not allowed:
https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/blob/master/src/modules/commander/commander.cpp#L3895-L3896

The result is that if the FMU crashes the mixer enters the MIX_FAILSAFE mode and sets zero commands for all outputs. Therefore the plane will crash. By allowing the OVERRIDE flag to be set the pilot could at least try to land the plane in the manual mode.

title: Mixer of Bormatec Maja not working in Manual Override
body:
While testing the v1.6.5 of the PX4 I found the following issue:

During normal flight operation everything works as expected. In case of an FMU crash in the manual flight mode the OVERRIDE flag is correctly set in the px4io. However, in this mode the outputs for MAIN 1, MAIN 3 through MAIN 5 are correctly set. But the MAIN 2 (right aileron) output remains always at 1500 which corresponds to a zero deflection.

This behavior can be solved by removing the lines for the airbrakes ([L24](https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/blob/master/ROMFS/px4fmu_common/mixers/AAERTWF.main.mix#L24), [L29](https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/blob/master/ROMFS/px4fmu_common/mixers/AAERTWF.main.mix#L29)), or changing the index from 6 to a value lower than 4. However, I was not able to identify why an index value of 6 or higher breaks the mixing.

See also this topic in the [forum](http://discuss.px4.io/t/failsafe-in-case-of-an-fmu-crash-for-an-airplane/4209/5).

title: BUG on EKF2 when the PX4Flow goes invalid
body:
### **Bug Report**

**LOG:** https://logs.px4.io/plot_app?log=962b0f4e-3553-4ec2-b398-40258c9286e5

**Explanation:**
The PX4Flow is only valid at 35cm of the floor. 

To reproduce, handheld the UAV for some seconds over 50cm so we get a position then let the UAV on the ground.  After some minutes, take it over the ground again and you'll see that the position is completely off.

Note: In the log, you can see the handheld parts with the accelerometer.

**Anomalies in the log:**

* The two first handheld parts where with some rotation yet the third one (at 10') was without clear rotation.
* High yawrate while one the ground (4' - 10') 
* Peak in LPOS.x and LPOS.y (We don't see much because of that peak)
* We don't have the same peak with the distance sensor!
* Velocities are high while on the ground
* At 10', while handheld (almost not moving) the velocities tend to go up.


**Versions:**
* PX4 Firmware: 1.6.5
* Flow Firmware: QGC provided firmware (PX4/Flow/master)
* EKF_AID_MASK set to PX4Flow

**Workaround:** Using the PR https://github.com/PX4/Flow/issues/96 so the PX4Flow report is always marked as valid.

Original issue: https://github.com/PX4/Flow/issues/97

@sanderux I'm currently revising the battery estimation here https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/pull/8153.
It's currently broken in several ways according to my opinion. Not sure if your case is covered in my fixes, let's investigeate.

On the first glance it looks to me as if your battery estimation is always corrected using the thrust and for the factor of how much this is done you can use the parameter `BAT_V_LOAD_DROP`. You even say it does not change when setting an internal resistance.

What you should also know is that the current estimation always adjusts the empty cell voltage for any load which results in rescaling the whole calculation. I correct the voltage measurement itself (**only** for the remaining capacity estimation) in my pr... If you feel like and have time you can test my pr as soon as I fixed the CI stuff and pushed the newest enhancements today. **EDIT:** I made my changes

title: Solo PREFLIGHT FAIL: MAG SENSORS INCONSISTENT
body:
Hello,
I'm not sure if this could be an issue report, but I will post the problem here as I could not find any info on PX4Disscuss, or on other github repositories.

I am now working on flying 3DR Solo indoor with VICON for research.
As I googled and came to a conclusion that PX4 is the solution to incorporate VICON data using MavRos, and not Ardupilot (I hope this is true).  
So I flashed PX4 with `make px4fmu-v3_default`, as lpe version could not be found for v3 (Pixhawk2). 

The problem I got was not with mocap, but with magnetometer. 
Even If I calibrate, I always get `PREFLIGHT FAIL: MAG SENSORS INCONSISTENT` on qgroundcontrol.
According to [PX4 Tutorial](https://dev.px4.io/en/tutorials/pre_flight_checks.html), sensors inconsistent means it needs to calibrate, but I tried few times.
I am suspecting the orientation setting. As I searched on the web, Solo has HMC 5983, LSM303D onboard, and HMC 5983 for external magnetometer, and the orientation of onboard sensors is `pitch 180` and that of external is `Yaw293Pitch68Roll90`, however `Yaw293Pitch68Roll90` is not on the list in qgroundcontrol (please see an image below). 
As `Yaw293Pitch68Roll90` was prepared in `src/lib/conversion/rotation.cpp`, I thought by setting `CAL_MAG0_ROT` to 30 would work, but not successful.

title: PX4 1.6.5 Stbl: Loiter switching BUG.
body:
Hi guys,

We've had a total crash with a Skywalker, Plain Airplane profile. PX4 ver 1.6.5 stable.

https://logs.px4.io/plot_app?log=6daee88d-90d7-4cbe-abb7-440591fef87d

I think I found the reason but it is very strange and I need conformation. This is due to a BUG if I'm correct so please can you take a look and confirm the reason.

The pilot is not novice, it is pretty experienced one in terms of piloting a plane, but somehow sometimes the PX4 is overwhelming for him especially in certain situation and he is doing irrational switching (as many PX4 users might do).

This is the case:

He flew in Position and went in to Loiter (Pause). Then at some point he wanted to gain altitude while in Pause mode. In the graph it is obvious he started pitching up. But nothing happened as it should be, the plain continued to control the speed and throttle in the Loiter, despite the throttle lever was at 60%.  In the latest implementation the Pause button will get the plane in Loiter from any mode. So initially he was in Position mode with activated Position switch. Absolutely normal operation as it is meant to be. Then strangely enough he switched to Manual in the attempt to gain altitude, without turning off the Pause button. The plane continued to circle, but strangely enough transferred the full control of the Throttle to the lever of the RC instead of controlling the throttle in the loiter itself automatically. At the same time the pilot continued to pitch up and gained altitude and I see it clearly in the graphics.. Because he had the lever at 60% throttle it was not enough to sustain the loiter, so the plane started stalling, but still trying to continue to sustain the loiter radius and gain altitude in the condition of under throttle. Because of the stalls the plane was rather going in spirals toward the pilot, and he explained that he thought it is drifting still not realizing what is going on. He did not realize that the Throttle is in his control. Then at the last stall the plane just plunged in nose dive. Because we have a hard limit of 45deg for the pitch, the plane did not have any altitude and time to recover. 

I did not see any mechanical failure, neither to the servos neither to the GPS nor the airspeed sensor nor anything else.

Please can you confirm this and if it is a BUG it should be corrected. 

Pause should be totally Auto mode, probably allowed to have some small amount of pitch control in order to gain or loose altitude, but in no case we have to give the throttle a manual control at this moment.

[issue_comment] priseborough | created=2017-12-04T11:22:31Z | updated=2017-12-04T11:22:31Z | https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/issues/8400#issuecomment-348934180
We are dealing with the both the handling of 'home' and 'EKF origin' which have different uses.

The EKF origin's primary purpose is to enable NED local position data to be converted to global WGS-84 coordinates. The primary purpose of home is to provide a location for RTL recovery. 

If the vehicle takes off before the EKF has started using GPS, the EKF WGS-84 origin will be set at the horizontal position where the vehicle was when EKF internal GPS checks passed. The vertical position of the origin will be set to the estimated height of the takeoff point by subtracting distance above origin from the GPS height. This does not involve a height reset because the EKF local vertical position does not change when the EKF origin is set. Prior to the origin being set, no global position messages are published so flight in auto mode is not possible. 

The existing code set sets the home lat,lon,alt using the vehicle global position and does not correct for vehicle height above origin. Home local coordinates are set to vehicle local position.  https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/blob/master/src/modules/commander/commander.cpp#L1250-L1258. This is going to cause problems with RTL unless the local vertical position at takeoff is recorded and used to adjust the home alt for the vehicle height above origin. The other problem which cannot be worked around is that the vehicle will RTL to wherever it was when checks passed which will be unknown to the operator and is therefore unsafe. Until we introduce a method for the operator to confirm, adjust and approve the home location, we should disable RTL_STATE_LAND if home was set after takeoff.

In reference to the height datum issue, we could add a class variable _ref_alt_is_global to record if _ref_alt was set when vehicle_local_position.z_global was true  and if entering a waypoint controlled mode, reset _ref_alt to vehicle_local_position.ref_alt if (!_ref_alt_is_global && vehicle_local_position.z_global).

title: [Multicopter mixer] Wrongly computed mixing tables
body:
I was checking the new [mixer generator](https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/blob/master/src/lib/mixer/geometries/tools/px_generate_mixers.py) script from @jlecoeur  in order to add my specific multicopter geometry and I found that it produces values that didn't match my mixing table generated by a custom script.
After checking the generator, I found that the table generated doesn't match the mixing strategy used in PX4.
The table generated has the following coefficients for each actuator:
```
roll_gain | pitch_gain | yaw_gain | thrust_gain
``` 
And has to be used like this: 
`out = roll_gain*roll + pitch_gain*pitch + yaw_gain*yaw + thrust_gain*thrust` (which is the standard matrix*vector multiplication)
However, in PX4, the equation is 
`out = (roll_gain*roll + pitch_gain*pitch + yaw_gain*yaw + thrust)*out_gain` 
https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/blob/26d95ef67479b90212f5ea8255d43721865ff904/src/lib/mixer/mixer_multirotor.cpp#L188-L192

At the current state, there is a confusion and the `thrust_gain` generated in the tables is used as the `out_gain` which lead to an incorrect mixing and produces unexpected coupling between the axes.

This can be corrected in two different ways:
1. Fix the generator script to match firmware implementation
2. Change the PX4 implementation to use a simple matrix-style mixer

Since the gain of each motor can be chosen in the geometry config file, and that the matrix-style mixing table is simpler and more intuitive, I would prefer to use the 2nd alternative.
FYI @MaEtUgR @jlecoeur

title: Incorrect handling of baud rate values in RTPS
body:
**Bug Report**

This is a problem with the fast RTPS code. 

For both client and agent code, baud rate values are generated from the program argument by converting the argument directly to a number. However in termios.h, the baud rate is encoded in a number of preset values, eg B57600. This affects the agent running on Ubuntu since the encoded value is different from the actual baud rate. As a result executing the following in Ubuntu terminal:
./micrortps_agent -b 57600 -d /dev/ttyUSB1
results in this failure message:
UART transport: device: /dev/ttyUSB1; baudrate: 57600; sleep: 1us; poll: 0ms

ERR SET BAUD /dev/ttyUSB1: 0 (22)
Close UART
EXITING...

With the problem corrected using an extra function to convert the baud rate to the encoded value, the behaviour shown in the  terminal is:
UART transport: device: /dev/ttyUSB1; baudrate: 57600; sleep: 1us; poll: 0ms

no flush
sensor_combined publisher started

Note that there may be a separate problem with the code generation for the agent application. To obtain the above result, the agent software was generated using a modified msg/tools/generate_microRTPS_bridge.py script with the following diff:

```diff
53,54c53,59
<     if dir[0] != '/':
<         dir = root_path + "/" + dir
---
>     if len(dir)>0:
>         if dir[0] != '/':
>             dir = root_path + "/" + dir
>     else:
>         dir = root_path
> 
>     print "dir returned from get_absolute_path",dir
66c71
< parser.add_argument("-t", "--topic-msg-dir", dest='msgdir', type=str, nargs=1, help="Topics message dir, by default msg/", default="msg")
---
> parser.add_argument("-t", "--topic-msg-dir", dest='msgdir', type=str, nargs=1, help="Topics message dir, by default msg/", default="")
```

title: Manual control setpoint pitch is inverted
body:
Pitch is [commonly defined](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/7/7e/Rollpitchyawplain.png) as the righthand rotation around the y axis. Any variable (especially those which are used for inter-app communication) should adhere to this standard.

In the current master branch the field `pitch` of [manual_control_setpoint_s](https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/blob/master/src/modules/uORB/topics/manual_control_setpoint.h) is inverted.

It seems that the change was introduced with commit 1d5f62d890d1d85cef5e0f8e282d8e9e70717d46 [starting from here.](https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/commit/1d5f62d890d1d85cef5e0f8e282d8e9e70717d46#diff-b2cdb687c37812923ec65dc8fc767506L1400)

Before the commit the pitch value was mapped from the RC value with:

```
/*
* pitch input - stick down is negative, but stick down is pitching up (pos) in NED,
 * so reverse sign.
*/
manual_control.pitch = limit_minus_one_to_one(-1.0f * _rc.chan[_rc.function[PITCH]].scaled);
```

afterwards/now it is mapped with

```
manual_control.pitch = get_rc_value(PITCH, -1.0, 1.0);
```

so the previous correct sign change got lost.

Because the current state is confusing and wrong we have to either _rename_ the name of the variables in manual_control_setpoint_s or we have to _revert the sign change_. I am in favor of reverting the sign change.

I found the following commits related to the above change (directly after 1d5f62d890d1d85cef5e0f8e282d8e9e70717d46 in the commit history): 6f38ed3b4b6f266098d0616b6bd3c18ffe082755 e2ac5222d812bdbfaf33fc2d320ee22ab861d433 ef8b97437342401a464bcc844d6c347c33919d73

I tested with HIL and a VTOL model what happens when the SD card access starts to block during a mission, with similar, but not quite the same results as @JohnSnowball experienced:

- navigator blocks too after reaching the next waypoint, trying to access dataman. The vehicle starts to loiter around the last waypoint (flying a circle, as opposed to an "8")
- RTL does not work anymore
- mavlink connection still works, including mode switching and virtual joystick. However when QGC loads the mission from the vehicle (for example by restarting QGC and switching to the plan view), the mavlink receiver starts to block, and you cannot switch modes via QGC anymore, but you still receive the mavlink stream (datalink not lost).

title: EKF2 with optical flow drifts without flow data
body:
So I have been bench-testing a vehicle with a PX4Flow sensor + EKF2. `EKF2_AID_MASK` is set to fuse Flow and GPS. `EKF2_OF_QMIN` is set to 50.

When the vehicle is on the ground (PX4Flow lens blocked), the position estimate from EKF2 keeps drifting around, even the though the flow module returns 0 `quality` and 0 `integrated_x` and `integrated_y`. Here is a log from boot : https://logs.px4.io/plot_app?log=6628dc88-c567-4796-95a6-f0815ab1a535

Would be great if you could have a look @priseborough @ChristophTobler!

This is by design. Flow is always fused, but if on ground and quality metric is too low, motion compensated flow data is set to zero. See reply in https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/issues/9398.

rand() returns a integer and x1 and x2 are supposed to be from a uniform random distribution between +- 1.0 so so lines  522 and 523 should be

     x1 = 2.0 * ((double)rand() / (double)RAND_MAX) - 1.0;
     x2 = 2.0 * ((double)rand() / (double)RAND_MAX) - 1.0;
